- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply +0.8–1.2% bias to forecast for 30d.
- When sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.3–0.7% for next 5–7 days to capture sentiment reversal.
